Get started

Source: vignettes/get-started.Rmd
get-started.Rmd
library(tidypptsda)

Example datasets

Two example datasets ship with the package, one per station type. They are raw station exports, before any processing.

Internal helpers

Small internal tools shared by every function of the package:

  • verbosity: every exported function has verbose = 0/1/2 (silent / summary / details). Messages go through ppt_msg().
  • input checks: as_dt() always returns a copy, so user objects are never modified; check_cols() reports missing columns.
  • per-pig fitting: fit_by_pig() runs a function on each pig. A pig that fails is recorded and skipped instead of stopping everything.
  • removal log: new_removed() builds the removed table returned by every analysis step.
  • result object: new_ppt_result() gives every calc_*() function the same return structure.

qc_config

All quality-control thresholds live in one object created by qc_config(). Any single parameter can be overridden.

# Default settings
qc <- qc_config()
qc$duration_max
#> [1] 3600

# Override single parameters
qc_config(stage_range = c(40, 110), weight_outlier = c("rlm", "loess", "sd"))
#> 
#> ── QC settings ──
#> 
#> Station transfer
#>   max_gap_days: 3
#>   max_overlap_days: 1
#>   max_jump_kg: 10
#> Body weight records
#>   weight_range: 15, 150
#>   adapt_days: 7
#>   weight_track: TRUE
#>   track_tol: 0.08
#>   weight_outlier: rlm , loess, sd
#>   outlier_combine: any
#>   rlm_cutoff: 0.5
#>   sd_max: 3
#>   loess_span: 0.75
#> Pig-level checks
#>   min_records: 20
#>   min_test_days: 35
#>   max_missing_rate: 0.3
#>   entry_weight_max: 65
#>   exit_weight_min: 85
#>   track_flag_share: 0.4
#>   smooth_r2_min: 0.99
#> Growth and ADG
#>   stage_range: 40, 110
#>   curve_model: poly2
#>   max_extrap_days: 30
#> Feeder errors
#>   fiv_range: -20, 2000
#>   fiv0_abs_max: 20
#>   duration_max: 3600
#>   speed_fiv_lo_max: 500
#>   speed_strict_max: 110
#>   speed_range: 2, 170
#>   idle_duration_max: 500
#>   trough_diff_range: -20, 1800
#>   max_unidentified_feed_kg: 90
#>   fiv_max_by_weight: NULL (off)
#> Daily feed intake
#>   dfi_range: 0, 6
#>   dfi_quantile: NULL (off)
#>   dfi_correct: lmm
#>   impute_method: loess_lm
#>   long_gap_days: 3
#> Confidence flags
#>   max_edge_extrap_days: 15
#>   min_coverage: 0.7
#>   bin_width: 10
#>   min_bin_coverage_kg: 6
#>   bin_fcr_limits: NULL (off)

read_station

read_station() reads one or many station export files (or a whole folder) and returns one standard table: the same column names, types and units for NEDAP and FIRE, ready for [prep_visits()].

Which column of the export holds which field is described by a station format. The package has a built-in format for each station type, so the usual exports need no setup. For an export with other column names or positions (another software version, Chinese headers, another device), write the format once as a small tab-separated file and pass it with format. station_format("fire", file = "fire_format.txt") writes the built-in format as a template to start from.

# Write the example data to two CSV files, then read them back
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "fire_export")
dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 101, ], file.path(folder, "fire_101.csv"))
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 102, ], file.path(folder, "fire_102.csv"))

raw <- read_station(folder)
#> 
#> ── Reading 2 files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ Detected station type "fire"
#> ✔ Read 9794 rows from 2 files (FIRE)
head(raw)
#>    responder location          entry_time           exit_time duration

#> 1:     35877      101 2023-12-19 14:15:39 2023-12-19 14:18:02       NA

station_format

A station format says which column of an export holds which standard field, and in which unit. station_format() shows the built-in format of a station type and writes it as a template file for other exports.

station_format("nedap")
#>          field      column   unit required              description
#>         <char>      <char> <char>   <lgcl>                   <char>
#> 1:   responder   responder      -     TRUE       Transponder number
#> 2:    location    location      -     TRUE      Station (feeder) ID
#> 3:  entry_time  visit_time      -     TRUE            Entrance time
#> 4:   exit_time           -      -    FALSE                Exit time
#> 5:    duration    duration      s    FALSE          Occupation time
#> 6: feed_intake feed_intake      g     TRUE Feed intake of the visit
#> 7:      weight      weight   auto     TRUE              Body weight
#> 8:       breed       breed      -    FALSE                    Breed
station_format("fire")
#>           field       column   unit required                     description
#>          <char>       <char> <char>   <lgcl>                          <char>
#>  1:   responder          Tag      -     TRUE              Transponder number
#>  2:    location     Location      -     TRUE             Station (feeder) ID
#>  3:  entry_time   Date,Entry      -     TRUE                   Entrance time
#>  4:   exit_time    Date,Exit      -     TRUE                       Exit time
#>  5: feed_intake     Consumed     kg     TRUE        Feed intake of the visit
#>  6:      weight       Weight     kg     TRUE                     Body weight
#>  7:   trough_in       Ent Wt     kg     TRUE       Trough weight at entrance
#>  8:  trough_out       Ext Wt     kg     TRUE           Trough weight at exit
#>  9:       topup Topup Amount     kg    FALSE Feed dispensed during the visit
#> 10:       breed        breed      -    FALSE                           Breed

# Write a template, edit it, and use it
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
station_format("fire", file = f)
#> ✔ Station format written to /tmp/Rtmpm6KhRd/file1cf83d98d01a.txt
cat(readLines(f), sep = "\n")
#> # tidypptsda station format: FIRE
#> # One line per field, separated by tabs: field, column, unit.
#> # column: column name or position; alternatives with |; date,time joined with ,; - if absent.
#> # unit: kg / g / auto for masses, s / min for duration, - or a strptime format for times.
#> # Required fields: responder, location, entry_time, exit_time, feed_intake, weight, trough_in, trough_out.
#> field    column  unit
#> responder    Tag -
#> location Location    -
#> entry_time   Date,Entry  -
#> exit_time    Date,Exit   -
#> feed_intake  Consumed    kg
#> weight   Weight  kg
#> trough_in    Ent Wt  kg
#> trough_out   Ext Wt  kg
#> topup    Topup Amount    kg
#> breed    breed   -
unlink(f)

prep_visits

prep_visits() turns the output of read_station() (or a raw NEDAP or FIRE export already in R, such as the example datasets) into one standard visit table that every later step uses:

  • one row per visit, including unidentified visits (no transponder read), marked with identified = FALSE. They are needed to compute the differences between subsequent visits on a feeder (Casey et al. 2005);
  • the same column names and units for both stations: body weight in kg, feed intake and trough weights in g, times as POSIXct (UTC);
  • FIRE visits that cross midnight get the right exit time;
  • a body weight of 0 becomes NA;
  • pigs seen at more than one station are kept (see Station transfer).
visits <- prep_visits(fire)

#> • Duplicated rows (dropped): 0
#> ℹ No pig was seen at more than one station
#> ✔ 26 pigs at 2 stations, 9794 visits over 66 days
#> ℹ No breed column. To use breed in the feed intake model and breed-specific limits, add it with `add_breed()`.

add_breed

Pig breed (or line) usually is not in the station export and cannot be read from the transponder number. add_breed() merges a breed table from your own records into the visit table. With a breed column:

  • calc_adfi() adds breed as a fixed effect to the correction model;
  • fiv_max_by_weight limits can differ by breed;
  • calc_fcr() summarises traits by breed.
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
# a breed table from your own herd records, one row per pig
pigs <- unique(visits[identified == TRUE, responder])
breeds <- data.frame(responder = pigs, breed = rep(c("YY", "LL"), length.out = length(pigs)))
visits <- add_breed(visits, breeds)
#> ✔ Breed added for 30 of 30 pigs: LL (15), YY (15)
table(unique(visits[identified == TRUE, .(responder, breed)])$breed)
#> 
#> LL YY 
#> 15 15

clean_weight

clean_weight() cleans the body weight records of identified visits in three layers:

  1. record rules: weights outside weight_range and weights of the adaptation period (adapt_days) are flagged;
  2. outlier detection per pig: the weight is first tracked back from the end of the test (weight_track); then one or more methods fit a curve to the remaining records of each pig and flag records far from it:
    • "rlm" (default): quadratic robust regression with bisquare weights (MASS::rlm), records with weight below rlm_cutoff are outliers;
    • "loess" (default): robust LOESS (family = "symmetric"), residuals beyond sd_max robust SDs;
    • "stl": STL decomposition of the daily median weight (weekly period, robust), residuals beyond sd_max robust SDs. Falls back to LOESS for pigs with fewer than 14 days;
    • "sd": quadratic least squares, residuals beyond sd_max SDs;
  3. pig checks: number of valid records, test length, missing rate, entry and exit weight, share removed by the tracking and the R of the LOESS smooth.

Nothing is deleted silently: every record keeps a qc_flag, and every removed pig is listed in removed with the reason.

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits)
#> 
#> ── Cleaning body weight (rlm + loess) ──────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Weight records: 31,472
#> • Outside weight range: 0
#> • Adaptation after entry (not used): 3,404
#> • Outliers: 5,667
#> •  of which removed by tracking: 1,543
#> ! Pigs kept: 28, low confidence: 1, removed: 1
w
#> 
#> ── <ppt_weight> ──
#> 
#> Pigs: 30 (keep 28, low confidence 1, removed 1)

#> $records: 31472 rows x 10 columns

# Why pigs were removed

# Records flagged as outliers

calc_adg

calc_adg() estimates average daily gain (ADG) over the body weight stage stage_range (default 30-120 kg):

  1. a growth curve is fitted to the valid weight records of each pig (curve_model: "poly2" by default, "poly1", "poly3" or "gompertz"; Gompertz falls back to a quadratic curve when it does not converge);
  2. the stage end is the first time the curve reaches the upper stage weight; the stage start is the last time the curve rises through the lower stage weight before that. A curve that dips back below 30 kg (for example after noisy early records) therefore starts the stage only once the pig has really entered it. The search runs up to max_extrap_days before the first and after the last record;
  3. every day of the stage gets a body weight: the daily median of the valid records ("observed"); a day without valid weight between two recorded days is filled by linear interpolation ("interpolated"); a day before the first or after the last recorded day is filled by the growth curve ("curve");
  4. ADG = slope of the linear regression of these daily weights on the day, over the stage days. Its R tells how straight the growth was.

Every pig gets an adg_type:

  • "observed": both stage limits are reached inside the recorded period;
  • "extrapolated": at least one limit needs extrapolation, but no more than max_extrap_days;
  • "partial": a limit is not reached even after extrapolation. ADG is then computed over the part of the stage that is covered;
  • "none": less than 7 days of the stage are covered; ADG is NA.
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(w)
#> 
#> ── ADG over 30-120 kg (poly2 curve) ────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Observed (stage inside the records): 21
#> • Extrapolated: 7
#> • Partial (stage not fully reached): 1
#> • No ADG: 0
#> ! 1 pig does not reach the whole stage: ADG is based on part of it (adg_type = "partial").
#> ✔ Mean ADG: 1205 g/d (SD 133)
head(adg$per_pig[, .(responder, adg_type, start_date, end_date, stage_days, adg)])
#>    responder     adg_type start_date   end_date stage_days      adg
#>       <char>       <char>     <Date>     <Date>      <num>    <num>
#> 1:     13913     observed 2024-03-02 2024-05-16   75.56102 1209.897
#> 2:     13918     observed 2024-03-06 2024-05-24   78.43858 1162.966
#> 3:     13954 extrapolated 2024-03-10 2024-05-28   79.28093 1124.224
#> 4:     13996     observed 2024-02-28 2024-05-07   69.15285 1334.979
#> 5:     14962     observed 2024-02-26 2024-05-07   70.15055 1278.746
#> 6:     15006     observed 2024-02-28 2024-05-07   68.69428 1317.472

# Gompertz curve, with quadratic fallback
adg_g <- calc_adg(w, qc = qc_config(curve_model = "gompertz"), verbose = 0)
table(adg_g$per_pig$curve_used)
#> 
#> gompertz 
#>       29

# Source of the daily weights over the stage
table(adg$daily[in_stage == TRUE, source])
#> 
#>        curve interpolated     observed 
#>           35           12         2158

flag_feed_errors

flag_feed_errors() applies the 16 error criteria of Casey et al. (2005, Table 3) to every visit.

The seven variables are computed on the complete visit sequence of each feeder, including unidentified visits, sorted by entrance time:

  • FIV = feed intake per visit (g), OTV = occupation time (s), FRV = FIV / (OTV / 60) (g/min, not computed when OTV <= 0);
  • LWD = trough weight at entrance of the following visit - at exit of this visit; FWD = trough weight at entrance of this visit - at exit of the preceding visit (FIRE only, NEDAP has no trough weights);
  • LTD = entrance time of the following visit - exit time of this visit; FTD = entrance time of this visit - exit time of the preceding visit.
# Error Visits considered Threshold (default)
1 FIV-lo all FIV < -20 g
2 FIV-hi all FIV > 2000 g
3 FIV-0 OTV = 0 |FIV| > 20 g
4 OTV-lo all OTV < 0 s
5 OTV-hi all OTV > 3600 s
6 FRV-hi-FIV-lo 0 < FIV < 50 g FRV > 500 g/min
7 FRV-hi-strict FIV >= 50 g, preceding or following visit FIV < -20 g FRV > 110 g/min
8 FRV-hi FIV >= 50 g, neither neighbour FIV < -20 g FRV > 170 g/min
9 FRV-0 FRV = 0 OTV > 500 s
10 FRV-lo FRV != 0 |FRV| <= 2 g/min
11-12 LWD-lo / LWD-hi all but the last visit on the feeder LWD < -20 g / > 1800 g
13-14 FWD-lo / FWD-hi all but the first visit on the feeder FWD < -20 g / > 1800 g
15 LTD-lo all but the last visit LTD < 0 s
16 FTD-lo all but the first visit FTD < 0 s

The thresholds come from [qc_config()]. Feed disappearance in unidentified visits (-20 g <= FIV <= 2000 g) is summed per feeder; Casey et al. discarded pens above 90 kg, here a warning is given above max_unidentified_feed_kg.

visits <- prep_visits(fire, verbose = 0)
flagged <- flag_feed_errors(visits, verbose = 2)
#> 
#> ── Flagging feeder errors (Casey et al. 2005) ──────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ Visits with at least one error: 2.62% of 9743 identified visits
#> • FRV-lo: 64 (0.66%)
#> • LWD-hi: 60 (0.62%)
#> • FWD-hi: 60 (0.62%)
#> • FIV-lo: 33 (0.34%)
#> • FRV-hi: 28 (0.29%)
#> • FIV-hi: 21 (0.22%)
#> • LWD-lo: 5 (0.05%)
#> • FRV-hi-strict: 4 (0.04%)
#> • FWD-lo: 4 (0.04%)
#> • FRV-0: 1 (0.01%)
attr(flagged, "feeders")
#>    location n_visits n_unidentified unidentified_feed_kg error_rate
#>      <char>    <int>          <int>                <num>      <num>
#> 1:      101     6014             30                2.148 0.01788102
#> 2:      102     3780             21                0.621 0.03937217

calc_adfi

calc_adfi() estimates average daily feed intake (ADFI) over the same body weight stage as [calc_adg()], so that FCR compares like with like.

Correction (Jiao et al. 2014, after Casey et al. 2005): for each pig and day, the error-free intake y (sum of FIV over visits without error) is modelled with a linear mixed model fitted on all pig-days:

y ~ location + breed + BW + ADG + 16 x PTE + 11 x OTD + 4 x FID + (1 | pig)

  • PTE: share of the day’s visits with error type p; OTD: occupation time of visits with error p (types 1, 2, 6-14); FID: feed intake of visits with error p (types 4, 5, 15, 16);
  • BW: body weight of the day from [calc_adg()] (observed, interpolated or from the growth curve, column weight_filled); ADG of the pig;
  • location is a fixed effect when there is more than one station, and breed when the data have a breed column (see [add_breed()]) with more than one breed.

The corrected intake is y - sum(b x error covariates): only the effects of the error covariates are removed, so a day without errors keeps its recorded intake. Covariates without variation or perfectly collinear with others are dropped before fitting. Days on which every visit has an error have no error-free intake and are imputed.

Checks and imputation over the stage days of each pig:

  • corrected intake below 0, outside dfi_range, or outside the optional dfi_quantile limits is set to missing;
  • impute_method = "loess_lm" (default): a gap of up to long_gap_days
    1. days between recorded days is filled from a robust LOESS smooth of the daily intake over the days; a longer gap, and the days before the first or after the last recorded day, are filled by a per-pig linear regression of daily intake on body weight;
  • impute_method = "linear": linear interpolation between recorded days (whatever the gap length), the same regression on body weight at the ends.

Use [validate_adfi()] to compare both on your own data: precision depends mainly on how many days are missing at the stage ends, which is why such pigs are flagged by [calc_fcr()].

Day states: "org" (no error, recorded value), "corr" (corrected), "iii" (filled between recorded days), "elrp" (filled before the first or after the last recorded day), "missing".

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)

adg <- calc_adg(w, verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg)

calc_fcr

calc_fcr() combines ADG and ADFI, both computed over the same body weight stage, into the feed conversion ratio FCR = ADFI / ADG (kg feed per kg gain) and its inverse, feed efficiency G:F = ADG / ADFI.

Each pig gets fcr_flag = "ok" or "low_confidence", with the reasons in fcr_note: the growth curve or the feed intake extrapolated over more than max_edge_extrap_days (default 15) at the start or end of the stage, an inner 10 kg class with recorded weights spanning less than min_bin_coverage_kg (default 6 kg), a segment FCR outside the optional bin_fcr_limits, ADG on part of the stage only, less than min_coverage (default 0.7) of the stage with recorded feed intake, or weight data flagged by [clean_weight()].

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg, verbose = 0)
fcr <- calc_fcr(adg, adfi)
#> 
#> ── FCR over 30-120 kg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ FCR for 29 pigs: 23 ok, 6 low confidence
#> ✔ Mean FCR 2.36 (SD 0.14), ADG 1205 g/d, ADFI 2847 g/d
head(fcr$per_pig[, .(responder, adg, adfi, fcr, fcr_flag, fcr_note)])

plot_adg, plot_adfi and save_plots

One plot per station, one panel per pig. Axes adapt to the data and to stage_range, so no point is dropped. Colours come from a colour-blind safe palette (Okabe-Ito) without extra packages.

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(w, verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg, verbose = 0)

g <- plot_adg(adg, weight = w, locations = "101", responders = c("13913", "13918", "13954"))
#> ✔ Created 1 growth plot
g$plot[[1]]


f <- plot_adfi(adfi, responders = c("13913", "13918", "13954"))
#> ✔ Created 1 feed intake plot
f$plot[[1]]


out <- save_plots(g, path = tempdir(), prefix = "loc", suffix = "growth", device = "pdf")
#> ✔ Saved 1 of 1 plot to /tmp/Rtmpm6KhRd
file.exists(out$file)
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(out$file)

run_pipeline

run_pipeline() runs every step with one set of QC settings and keeps all intermediate results.

res <- run_pipeline(fire, qc = qc_config(stage_range = c(60, 120)), verbose = 0)

write_results

write_results() writes the tables of an analysis to CSV files named <farm>_<table>_<date>.csv, ready to send to the testing station. Files are UTF-8 with a byte order mark so that Excel shows Chinese text correctly.

res <- run_pipeline(nedap, verbose = 0)
out <- write_results(res, dir = file.path(tempdir(), "results"), farm = "demo")
#> ✔ Wrote 9 files to /tmp/Rtmpm6KhRd/results
out

#>          <char>                                                 <char> <int>

validate_outliers, validate_adg and validate_adfi

Three functions check how well the methods work on your own data, by hiding or spoiling part of the data on purpose and measuring how close the result comes to what is known:

  • validate_outliers() adds artificial errors to clean weight records and measures how many each outlier method finds, how many good records it removes, and how much ADG is affected;
  • validate_adg() compares growth curve models by k-fold cross-validation on recorded days, and by how much ADG changes when the first or last days of the test are hidden (late entry, early exit);
  • validate_weight_fill() hides recorded daily weights of the stage (random days, blocks, start or end), fills them again with each weight fill method and compares the filled weights and ADG with the recorded ones;
  • validate_adfi() hides recorded feed intake days in the same way, imputes them again and compares ADFI with the recorded value.
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)

# 1. weight outlier methods: 5% artificial errors of 3-15 kg
vo <- validate_outliers(visits, reps = 1)
